entities.summary:
Ding Feng (丁奉), general of the state of Eastern Wu in the Three Kingdoms period of China, played a crucial role in the region's military campaigns and strategic alliances.

Born in the 3rd century AD, Ding Feng's rise to prominence was marked by his involvement in the Battle of Red Cliffs, a pivotal event that secured Eastern Wu's control over the Yangtze River.

As a skilled military leader, Ding Feng oversaw the development of Eastern Wu's navy, which enabled the region to challenge the dominance of the Wei state.

Ding Feng's legacy extends beyond his military accomplishments, as he also played a key role in promoting the cultural and economic prosperity of Eastern Wu.

His younger brother, Ding Feng (丁封), also served as a general in the state, while Ding Feng (丁峰), a professional sport shooter, bears a different surname but shares a similar name with the historical figure.

The Ding family's influence can be seen in the many historical records and artifacts that have survived to this day, providing a fascinating glimpse into the lives of these ancient Chinese leaders.

In the words of the famous Chinese historian, Ban Gu, 'Ding Feng was a general of great talent, who played a key role in the conquest of the Three Kingdoms.'

Ding Feng's remarkable achievements serve as a testament to the enduring legacy of the Three Kingdoms period, a time of great upheaval and transformation in Chinese history.
